newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Downer to visit South Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Downer to visit South Pacific.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer will make his first trip to the South Pacific next week since the embarrassing leak of a top secret paper which insulted Canberra's allies in the region.
Downer will travel to Vanuatu on Saturday, Fiji on Tuesday and will arrive in New Zealand on Friday for a regular biannual meeting with his counterpart Don McKinnon.

Government officials said on Thursday they were confident that Australia had regained the confidence of its South Pacific allies with Downer expected to devote little time to explaining his government's actions over the matter.
"I'm not sure exactly what they will discuss because these meetings will be private meetings between Mr Downer and leaders in those respective countries," one government official told reporters.

"But certainly the indications that we've had back so far are that these countries are moving forward in the relationship and that they have understood very clearly what the government's policy and attitudes and views are, and that's obviously not what was contained in those media stories."
Australian diplomats in the South Pacific have spent the past few weeks assuring their counterparts that the 93-page report did not reflect government policy.

The secret report, which described Vanuatu as being wracked by political instability and cronyism, was prepared as a briefing for Australian Treasurer Peter Costello for a summit of economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum in July.
The document was left on a table in a public area at the economic ministers' meeting, where it was obtained by Reuters.
South Pacific nations, such as Nauru and the Cook Islands, have said the report will damage Australia's relations with the region.
